Part of the Tn-seq workflow. The phage stock for a library must come from a single temperature-sensitive clone (forms plaques at 30 °C, not at 37 °C). Work with phage in a tissue-culture hood; wipe everything with bleach and ethanol, and put waste in biohazard bags. MP buffer: 50 mM Tris pH 7.5, 150 mM NaCl, 10 mM MgSO₄, 2 mM CaCl₂. Top agar(ose): 0.6% agarose; add 2 mM CaCl₂ after autoclaving; hold at 38–42 °C. Steps Plaque isolation. Wash stationary M. smegmatis (OD 0.5–6 all work) three times in MP buffer (6,000 × g, 2 min), resuspend in ~1/4 of the volume. Make 10-fold dilutions (10⁻¹–10⁻⁵) of the phage in MP buffer. Mix 4 mL top agar, 50 µL cells and 100 µL phage dilution, pour onto LB plates, incubate at 30 °C for 36–48 h. (Skip to step 3 if a temperature-sensitive isolate was prepared within the last two weeks.) Identify temperature-sensitive plaques. Make a cell lawn (4 mL top agar + 50 µL washed cells) on two LB plates; let dry ≥30 min (do not over-dry). Pick 8 plaques into 100 µL MP buffer each, spot 10–20 µL of each on both plates (one quadrant per plaque). Incubate one plate at 30 °C and one at 37 °C for 2 days. Use a plaque that grew only at 30 °C. Prepare the clone. Crush the agar plug of a temperature-sensitive plaque in 400 µL MP buffer, spin 5 min at high speed (parafilm the tube before taking it out of the hood), and pass the supernatant through a 0.2 µm filter. This is the new phage stock. Make 10-fold dilutions (10⁻¹–10⁻⁸), plate as in step 1 and incubate 2 days at 30 °C. Amplify. Choose the dilution that gives “lacy” (nearly confluent) plates. Pour 5 plates at that dilution; incubate 2 days at 30 °C. Because stocks degrade, it is safer to pour 10 plates: five at the lacy dilution and five at a 5-fold higher dilution. Collect. Flood each plate with 3 mL MP buffer and rock overnight at 4 °C. Collect, spin at high speed in the cold, and filter through 0.2 µm (change filters when they clog). Titer. Make 10-fold dilutions (10⁻¹–10⁻¹³). Spot 2 × 5 µL of each on lawn plates, let dry at least 30 min, incubate 2 days at 30 °C. Calculate. PFU/mL = average plaques per spot × 200 × 10^(dilution factor). For transduction you want about 5×10¹⁰ to 2×10¹¹ PFU/mL. Use amplified phage within about 3 days; make a fresh stock for each transduction. Versions Murry 2008-based M. smegmatis-optimized Host wash 7H9 + glycerol + ADC, no Tween MP buffer Plates 7H10 (amplification, 10 cm) or LB LB throughout Amplification plates 5 × 10 cm 7H10, ~2 days at 30 °C 5–10 plates, 2 days at 30 °C Collection 3 mL MP per plate, 0.2 µm filter same, overnight at 4 °C Shelf life not stated use within 3 days The Fortune-lab Benchling version (2022) differs in detail: host M. smegmatis mc²155, 3.5 mL top agarose with 200 µL washed cells and 50 µL phage dilution on 7H10 + glycerol + ADC (no Tween), 2 mL MP buffer per plate rocked ~4 h at room temperature, 10 µL spots for titering; “a good stock is >5×10¹⁰ PFU/mL”. Dry lawn plates well before spotting or the spots run together. Centrifuge speeds are given as rpm in some sources and ×g in others; convert for your rotor.

This is a condensed summary. The manufacturer’s user guide (Thermo Fisher Scientific, full user guide (PDF), publication number MAN0000062) is the authoritative source and includes control reactions, vector maps and troubleshooting. PCR product requirements The kit is designed for blunt-end PCR products from thermostable proofreading polymerases (for example Pfx, Phusion or Q5). Do not add 5′ phosphates to your primers; such products will not ligate into the vector. Use a 7–30 minute final extension to make sure products are completely extended. Check the product on an agarose gel for a single discrete band of the correct size, or gel-purify it. TOPO cloning reaction Reagent Volume Fresh PCR product 0.5–4 µL Salt solution 1 µL Water to a total of 5 µL pCR-Blunt II-TOPO vector 1 µL Final volume 6 µL Mix gently and incubate for 5 minutes at room temperature (22–23 °C), then put on ice. The reaction can be stored at −20 °C overnight. For routine subcloning, 30 seconds may be enough; for products longer than 1 kb, or pools of PCR products, longer incubation gives more colonies (up to 30 minutes). The salt solution (final 200 mM NaCl, 10 mM MgCl₂ for chemical transformation) increases the number of transformants. Transformation Use kanamycin (50 µg/mL) or low-salt LB with zeocin (25 µg/mL) plates, and prewarm the plates at 37 °C for 30 minutes. Use two plates per transformation. Chemically competent cells Add 2 µL of the TOPO reaction to a vial of competent cells and mix gently (do not pipette up and down). Incubate on ice for 5–30 minutes. Heat shock for 30 seconds at 42 °C without shaking, then return to ice. Add 250 µL room-temperature S.O.C. medium and shake horizontally at 200 rpm and 37 °C for 1 hour. Spread 10–50 µL on prewarmed selective plates (two different volumes, with 20 µL S.O.C. added to spread small volumes evenly). Incubate overnight at 37 °C. Electrocompetent cells. Dilute the TOPO reaction 4-fold in water first (6 µL reaction + 18 µL water) to prevent arcing, then add 2 µL to 50 µL of cells, transfer to a chilled 0.1 cm cuvette, electroporate, and add 250 µL S.O.C. Recover for at least 1 hour at 37 °C before plating as above. If arcing is a problem, reduce the voltage by 10%, reduce the load resistance to 100 Ω, or precipitate the reaction and resuspend in water. An efficient reaction produces several hundred colonies. Pick about 10 colonies. Analyzing transformants Grow 2–6 colonies overnight in LB with the selective antibiotic, saving the original colony by patching to a fresh plate. Isolate plasmid DNA and check by restriction digest for the insert and its orientation (use enzymes that cut once in the vector and once in the insert), or sequence with M13 forward and reverse primers. Alternatively, screen colonies directly by colony PCR with an M13 primer and an insert-specific primer; run restriction analysis in parallel the first time. For long-term storage, make a glycerol stock (0.85 mL culture + 0.15 mL sterile glycerol) at −80 °C.

For an individual mutant from a φMycoMarT7 library (see the Tn-seq overview). The idea is that a SacII-cut, re-ligated fragment containing the transposon can replicate as a plasmid in a pir+ host and carry the flanking genomic sequence with it. Presumably the transposon carries an R6K origin and kanamycin marker; confirm against the phMycoMarT7 map. Prepare genomic DNA with a quick prep that includes RNase (so the A₂₆₀ reading reflects DNA; see Smash and Grab or the long gDNA prep). Digest 2 µg gDNA with 3 µL SacII in 1× CutSmart buffer (3 µL), water to 30 µL, overnight at 37 °C. Heat-inactivate 20 min at 65 °C. Add 4 µL T4 DNA ligase buffer and 2 µL T4 DNA ligase; incubate overnight at 16 °C. Heat-inactivate 20 min at 65 °C. Reduce the volume to ~15 µL (speed-vac) and dialyze the DNA for 30 min. Electroporate into freshly made electrocompetent pir+ E. coli (BW25142; see E. coli electrocompetent cells). Pick colonies, grow in LB + kanamycin 50 µg/mL, miniprep. Sequence with the transposon primer that reads out of the transposon into the genome: 5′-GTCTAGAGACCGGGGACTTATC-3′ (the same transposon primer used for Tn-seq library PCR 1). Align the resulting sequence to the genome to find the insertion site.

1. Lysis (about 1.5 h) Grow a 10 mL M. smegmatis culture to late log (OD₆₀₀ 0.6–0.9). Pellet 5 min at 4 °C. Resuspend in 500 µL PBS + 1 mM PMSF (add PMSF from a 100 mM stock, 10 µL per mL of PBS). No Tween in the lysis PBS. Transfer to a bead-beating tube pre-filled with beads (to the bevel at the bottom of the tube). Bead-beat 2 min (balance the tubes symmetrically), then 5 min on ice. Repeat for 4 rounds in total. Spin 10 min at 16,000 rpm in the cold. Measure A₂₈₀ of a few µL of supernatant by NanoDrop (blank: PBS + PMSF). Record the concentration. Vortex supernatant and pellet back together. Add Laemmli to 1× (100 µL if the pellet was in 500 µL PBS). PgfA variant: also add 30 µL fresh 1 M DTT, heat 95 °C for 20 min. PonA1 variant: heat 95 °C for 10 min. Spin 1 min at 16,000 × g, room temperature. Move supernatants to new labeled tubes. Normalize all samples to the lowest concentration with PBS + Laemmli. The target is at least 10 mg/mL. Store at –20 °C. 2. Gel and transfer (about 3 h) Load at least 50–100 µg total protein in 15 µL (PgfA: precast NuPAGE-type gel; PonA1: homemade gel). Run at 35 mA for 45–60 min in 1× Tris-glycine-SDS buffer. Assemble the transfer sandwich, bottom to top: two sponges (pre-wet in transfer buffer), filter paper, gel, PVDF membrane, filter paper, 2–3 sponges. Wet PVDF in methanol until it is no longer glossy; handle only with tweezers. Cut off the stacking gel and the bottom ridge. Remove all bubbles (a little transfer buffer helps). For a tight pack use a third sponge or thick filter paper. Fill the tank with transfer buffer (below the screws) and the outer chamber with cold water. Put the whole unit in an ice bucket. Run at about 25 V for 60 min for one mini gel. Larger proteins need longer time or more voltage. 3. Blocking and antibodies (about 2.5 h) Disassemble, keeping track of lane order. Cut the top right corner off the membrane on the side that touched the gel, so you know which side to image. Block 30 min at room temperature in 10 mL TTBS + 5% milk (use a box that never held Coomassie). Wash 3 × 5 min with plain TTBS. Primary antibody in 10 mL TTBS: PgfA: 2 µL rabbit anti-PgfA, 1 h at room temperature (or overnight at 4 °C). Used dilutions can be saved at –20 °C and re-used. PonA1-tagged: cut the membrane so the upper part can be probed for a loading control (RpoB). Anti-GFP polyclonal at 33.3 µL per 10 mL; anti-RpoB re-used from a previous dilution. Save primary dilutions in labeled tubes at –20 °C. Wash 3 × 5 min with TTBS; leave 10 mL plain TTBS on the blot. Add 3 µL of secondary antibody (rabbit for the target, mouse for RpoB), 1 h at room temperature. Wash 3–5 × 5 min with TTBS. 4. Detection Add chemiluminescent reagent (PgfA: 500 µL of each component; PonA1: 250 µL of each in ~1 mL TTBS) and image immediately. Image the ladder with the colorimetric setting (auto exposure), then the bands with the chemiluminescence setting (auto or manual exposure). Save the raw chemiluminescence and ladder images separately. Merged images are not used for publication; keep raw files. If background is high, wash 3 × more in TTBS and re-image. Antibody dilutions are as written in the original notes. Confirm and express as ratios (e.g. 1:5000) for the public version. The two source protocols differ in details (heat time, DTT, reagent volume), as listed above. Variant: general blot for a Strep-tagged protein Differences from the protocol above: Lyse in 300–500 µL PBS + PMSF; keep the bead-beating pellet in case the protein is a transmembrane protein. Heat 95 °C for 10 min. Storing at –20 °C is fine. Load at least 70–85 µg (source says “mg”) protein on a 12% gel. Run 30 mA for 20 min, then ~35 mA once the sample is past the stacking gel. Transfer at 25 V for 60 min per mini gel; use 75–80 min for a ~28 kDa protein. Block 60 min at room temperature (or overnight at 4 °C) in TTBS + 5% milk. 5% BSA in PBS-Tween can lower background (filter through 0.22 µm first), but do not block with BSA when detecting a His-tagged protein.
